newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, cash slips.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, cash slips.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Thursday in quiet post-bidweek trade, with little conviction about direction and many sidelined waiting for clearer cash signs once February flows begin.
At 1425 EST, March edged up 1.7 cents to $2.455 per million British thermal units, while April was 2.4 cents higher at $2.18. Others were narrowly mixed.

"January cash got hammered this morning. I'm still optimistic because I think it's too early to discount winter," said one Houston-based trader, adding a sustained cold snap could still ignite a rally.

While colder forecasts for Northeast and Mid-Atlantic states next week may rouse the bulls, bears cite comfortable eastern stock levels and expectations for milder temperatures in Midcontinent and southern tier states.

And although technicians were looking for a brief rally from an extremely oversold market, few expected the upside to be sustained without better fundamentals. They pegged next support in March at the December low of $2.35 and then around $2.12. Resistance was seen at $2.70 and $2.80.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast prices notionally were talked Thursday about five cents lower in the $2.80s. Feb Midcon pipes were unchanged in the low-to-mid $2.70s. New York city gate gas for Feb delivery was quoted down slightly in the $3.50-60 range.
NYMEX said 18,869 Hub contracts traded by 1400 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1415 EST.
On KCBT, March climbed six cents to $2.20, while April ngaswas three cents higher at $1.91. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.3 cents to 25.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
